Cuenca: the cathedral’s blue domes above the city

After breakfast, transfer to the airport for your flight to the Galápagos Islands.

Your guide will meet you at Baltra Airport, help with your luggage and take you to the bus. It takes about 10 minutes to reach the Itabaca Channel, which separates Baltra from Santa Cruz. The motorboat crossing takes another 5 minutes or so.

From there, it’s about a 45-minute drive across Santa Cruz towards Puerto Ayora. The landscape changes noticeably along the way, from the red, rocky terrain of the north to the green highlands and the more humid south.

The group first visits the Santa Cruz highlands. Farmland borders wild terrain here, and the birds include the famous Galápagos finches associated with Charles Darwin’s research, along with other endemic species.

The main focus of the day is seeing giant land tortoises in their natural habitat. On private farms, you can see tortoises of different ages and sizes. Younger tortoises have smoother, shinier shells, while older animals bear the marks of a long life. Sometimes you can hear them tearing off leaves and chewing. Your guide will explain how privately run farms help conserve the tortoises and their habitat.

Next, visit the lava tunnels. They formed as lava flows cooled unevenly: the outer layer hardened while hot lava continued to flow inside. Some sections collapsed over time, but the remaining passages take about 30 minutes to walk through. Some stretches are high and wide, while fallen boulders make others harder to cross. The walls and solidified shapes show how the lava once flowed.

Lunch is included. After the excursion, transfer to the hotel and check in. You can spend the rest of the day walking around the port town of Puerto Ayora.

**Accommodation:** Villa Laguna 4*.  
**Meals:** breakfast, lunch.
